text:
Jonah (Design): quick review request 1: reworked the rollback confirm flow in the timeline. new microcopy + keyboard affordance idea: show inline 'Press R to rollback' hint on focused snapshot. adding mock in figma.
Priya (Eng): nice. question: is the shortcut global or scoped to the timeline? if global we risk collisions (R = reply in threads). recommend scoped when timeline has focus, and require modifier: Shift+R maybe.
Jonah (Design): intended scoped. visual hint only when snapshot card receives keyboard focus. no global listeners.
Karen (PM): microcopy thought: 'Rollback' feels scary. can we try 'Revert to snapshot' as primary action and keep 'Rollback' in the confirmation sentence for clarity? example: primary button label `Revert to snapshot` and body: "Are you sure you want to rollback to snapshot 2026-03-10 14:02?"
Leo (Accessibility): language is important. avoid verbs that are ambiguous. "Revert to snapshot" is more explicit for users. for SR: use 'Confirm revert to snapshot' for the dialog title. also ensure the shortcut hint is keyboard-only (visually hidden for SR users) and announced when the snapshot card receives focus: `aria-live="polite"` announcing 'Press Shift R to revert to this snapshot.'
Priya (Eng): implementation detail: we'll add a `data-shortcut="Shift+R"` attribute on the card and register a scoped listener on the timeline container. we should also ensure the action triggers an optimistic UI change only after the server returns success. API endpoint: POST /api/deploys/revert { snapshot_id }
Jonah (Design): about the confirmation modal itself 1: i'm trying a compact affordance that keeps the timeline context visible. is that ok from a11y standpoint?
Leo (Accessibility): compact modal can be okay if it's a true modal (focus trap, role=dialog) and we still provide a full-screen alternative for users who prefer reduced motion or larger targets. recommend keyboard nav order: heading -> descriptive text -> primary button -> secondary cancel. also include `aria-describedby` pointing to the snapshot metadata (time, user).
Karen (PM): add a small risk badge in the dialog if the revert will affect more than 10% of traffic. text: 'High impact: affects X% of users.' maybe red outline?
Jonah (Design): trying badge variants now. question on color contrast: our red  #d94848 on white fails AA at small text. suggestions?
Leo (Accessibility): either increase contrast by using a deeper red (#b02a2a) or use a darker border with white text on red background for the badge. also include an icon with `aria-hidden=true` and textual label visible to SR.
Priya (Eng): telemetry: when users press the keyboard shortcut, we should emit analytic event `ui.revert.shortcut` with {snapshot_id, focused=true}. confirm consent?
Karen (PM): yes capture that. also capture `ui.revert.confirm` with reason optional. we'll add param `reason=manual`/`auto` later.
Jonah (Design): copy tweaks: primary `Revert to snapshot` secondary `Cancel` and helper line: 'This will return traffic and configuration to the selected snapshot.' is that too wordy?
Leo (Accessibility): shorter is better. try: 'Reverts traffic and settings to this snapshot.' and use `aria-describedby` to include the full timestamp and author.
Priya (Eng): e2e note: add test case for keyboard shortcut and for SR announcement. also add one for high-impact badge rendering.
deploy-bot: canary-service: rollback gating check 1: all gates green. safe to revert if needed.
Karen (PM): decision for now: use `Revert to snapshot` label, scoped shortcut Shift+R, compact modal with full-screen fallback, high-impact badge variant B (darker red), analytic events as discussed. tagging eng for sprint 24.
Jonah (Design): thanks all, i'll upload updated frames and the aria snippet. attaching quick code sample: `
// on focus
card.addEventListener('focus', () => {
  srLive.textContent = 'Press Shift R to revert to this snapshot.'
  showVisualHint('Shift+R')
})

// keyboard handler
timeline.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
  if (e.shiftKey && e.code === 'KeyR' && document.activeElement.closest('.snapshot-card')) {
    openRevertDialog(document.activeElement.dataset.snapshotId)
  }
})
`
Jonah (Design): will follow up once figma and the ARIA snippet are in the thread. :sparkles:
